claim: Aging causes transcriptional drift, a phenomenon where genes within functional groups change expression in opposing directions.
source: Here, we uncover transcriptional drift, a phenomenon that describes how aging causes genes within functional groups to change expression in opposing directions.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on the study's results.

claim: Transcriptional drift causes a transcriptome-wide loss in mRNA stoichiometry in aging animals compared to young adults.
source: These changes cause a transcriptome-wide loss in mRNA stoichiometry and loss of co-expression patterns in aging animals, as compared to young adults.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a consequence of transcriptional drift.

claim: Extending lifespan by inhibiting serotonergic signals with mianserin attenuates transcriptional drift.
source: Using Caenorhabditis elegans as a model, we show that extending lifespan by inhibiting serotonergic signals by the antidepressant mianserin attenuates transcriptional drift, allowing the preservation of a younger transcriptome into an older age.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: Inhibition of serotonergic signals slows age-dependent physiological decline exclusively in young adults.
source: Our data are consistent with a model in which inhibition of serotonergic signals slows age-dependent physiological decline and the associated rise in mortality levels exclusively in young adults, thereby postponing the onset of major mortality.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Aging causes degeneration of tissues and organs, thereby increasing mortality due to systemic functional tissue failure.
source: Lifespan relates to aging, as the latter causes the degeneration of tissues and organs, thereby increasing mortality due to systemic functional tissue failure (Balch et al., 2008; Bishop et al., 2010; David et al., 2010; Haigis and Sweet-Cordero, 2011; Taylor and Dillin, 2011; Gladyshev, 2013; Burkewitz et al., 2015; Currais, 2015).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Mutations in age-1 or daf-2 slow degenerative processes occurring throughout life, thereby constantly lowering mortality rates.
source: Mutations in age-1 or daf-2, for example, slow degenerative processes occurring throughout life, thereby constantly lowering mortality rates (Johnson, 1990; Kenyon et al., 1993; Taylor et al., 2014).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Age-associated degenerative processes such as a decline in proteostatic capacity can be observed in young adults.
source: Age-associated degenerative processes such as a decline in proteostatic capacity are not necessarily restricted to older organisms but can also be observed in young adults (Labbadia and Morimoto, 2015a; 2015b).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Mianserin treatment reduced age-associated transcriptional drift across ~80% of the transcriptome.
source: Mianserin treatment reduced age-associated transcriptional drift across ~80% of the transcriptome, preserving many characteristics of transcriptomes of younger animals.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: Mianserin treatment extended lifespan by exclusively slowing age-associated changes in young adults.
source: We used transcriptional drift along with mortality analysis as metrics to monitor aging and find that mianserin treatment extended lifespan by exclusively slowing age-associated changes in young adults, thereby postponing the onset of mortality.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: Many GO annotations were enriched for both genes that increased as well as decreased in expression in response to mianserin.
source: We observed that many GOs were enriched for both, genes that increased as well as decreased as a consequence of aging.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this observation from the data analysis.

claim: As animals age, genes within functional groups change expression in opposing directions, disrupting relative mRNA ratios.
source: These charts suggested that as animals age and become older, genes change expression in opposing directions, disrupting relative mRNA ratios within the GO, when compared to young adults (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this observation, referencing Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mianserin treatment attenuated age-associated gene expression changes in over 90% of cases for 3,367 genes that significantly changed from day 1 to day 3.
source: Analyzing cohort #1 showed a significant change in expression levels of 3,367 genes, as the animals aged from day 1 to day 3, and a change in 5,947 genes from day 1 to day 10 (FDR < 0.1) (Figure 1g, significant genes only). Mianserin treatment reduced these age-associated expression changes in over 90% of cases.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 1g.

claim: Mianserin treatment attenuated age-associated changes in transcription in 15,095 out of 19,169 genes (80%, binomial P < 10–100).
source: Including all age-associated expression changes for the 19,196 different transcripts present in our data-set, we found that mianserin treatment attenuated age-associated changes in transcription in 15,095 out of 19,169 genes (80%, binomial P < 10–100).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with statistical support.

claim: Excluding genes that changed due to age and were attenuated by mianserin revealed a smaller gene-set enriched for GOs related to stress, xenobiotic and immune-responses, as well as genes associated with aging and the determination of lifespan.
source: When we excluded all genes that changed due to age and were attenuated by mianserin, we obtained a much smaller gene-set consisting of mianserin-induced changes that was enriched for GOs related to stress, xenobiotic and immune-responses, as well as genes associated with aging and the determination of lifespan (Table 1, Figure 1—source data 5).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Table 1 and Figure 1—source data 5.

claim: Drift-variance increases with age across the whole transcriptome in C. elegans.
source: We constructed drift-plots for all 19,196 genes in the data of cohort #1, which revealed a dramatic increase in drift-variance with age, showing a progressive loss of mRNA stoichiometries and co-expression patterns observed in young-adults (Figure 2a, shaded region encompassing the whiskers of Tukey-plot).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2a.

claim: Mianserin treatment attenuated the effect of aging across the whole transcriptome and preserved the co-expression patterns observed in young-adults into later age.
source: Mianserin treatment attenuated the effect of aging across the whole transcriptome and preserved the co-expression patterns observed in young-adults into later age.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Each subsample of ~1,000 genes showed identical increases in drift-variance with age, confirming a transcriptome-wide effect.
source: To test whether transcriptional drift is driven by a small subset of mRNAs or a transcriptome-wide phenomenon, we randomly divided the transcriptome into subsamples of ~1,000 genes. Each subsample showed identical increases in drift-variance with age, confirming a transcriptome-wide effect (Figure 2—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2—figure supplement 1f.

claim: Increasing doses of mianserin progressively increased longevity and decreased drift-variance as measured in 5-day-old animals.
source: Increasing doses of mianserin progressively increased longevity and decreased drift-variance as measured in 5-day-old animals (Figure 2b,c; Table 2).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2b,c and Table 2.

claim: Mianserin did not attenuate transcriptional drift-variance when added on day 5 of adulthood.
source: Mianserin did not attenuate transcriptional drift-variance when added on day 5 (Figure 2d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2d.

claim: Adding mianserin on day 3 of adulthood caused a small extension of lifespan and a corresponding small attenuation of drift-variance.
source: Adding mianserin on day 3 of adulthood caused a small extension of lifespan and a corresponding small attenuation of drift-variance, further supporting a quantitative relationship between suppression of drift-variance and extension of lifespan (Figure 1a, cohort #3, Figure 2d,e; Table 2).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 1a, Figure 2d,e, and Table 2.

claim: Mianserin fully induced the xenobiotic response by up to 1,000-fold irrespective of whether added on day 1 or day 5.
source: However, mianserin fully induced the xenobiotic response by up to 1,000-fold irrespective of whether added on day 1 or day 5 (Figure 2f).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2f.

claim: Treatment with daf-2 RNAi attenuated drift-variance in C. elegans.
source: Analyses of drift-variance for these data-sets showed that treatment with daf-2 RNAi attenuated drift-variance (Figure 2g).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2g.

claim: Mianserin and daf-2 RNAi attenuated age-associated drift of overlapping sets of genes (58% of 6,958 genes, binomial P= 6.3e-47).
source: Moreover, mianserin and daf-2 RNAi attenuated age-associated drift of overlapping sets of genes. Of the 6,958 genes for which expression levels were detected at all ages in both data-sets, 58% (4,078 genes, binomial P= 6.3e-47) were attenuated by both longevity-extending mechanisms.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with statistical support.

claim: Suppressing longevity by daf-16(RNAi) prevented the attenuation of drift-variance by daf-2(RNAi) and increased it beyond what was seen in control animals.
source: Conversely, suppressing longevity by daf-16(RNAi) prevented the attenuation of drift-variance by daf-2(RNAi) and increased it beyond what was seen in control animals (Figure 2g).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2g.

claim: Mianserin treatment preserved low drift-variance in transcriptomes and preserved longevity.
source: The results above suggested that preserving low drift-variance in transcriptomes preserves longevity.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Mianserin treatment increased the overall expression of oxidative stress response genes relative to age-matched controls.
source: We therefore constructed drift plots for redox-associated pathways that showed that mianserin indeed increased the overall expression of oxidative stress response genes (type I) relative to age-matched controls but also attenuated transcriptional drift (type II) (Figure 3b; Table 3).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 3b and Table 3.

claim: On day 3 of adulthood, no difference in stress resistance between mianserin-treated and untreated animals was observed.
source: On day 3 of adulthood, no difference in stress resistance between mianserin-treated and untreated animals was observed.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this observation.

claim: As animals grew older (day 5 and day 10), mianserin treatment greatly improved stress resistance.
source: As animals grew older (day 5 and day 10), mianserin treatment greatly improved stress resistance (Figure 3c; Table 4).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 3c and Table 4.

claim: Delaying the start of mianserin treatment to day 3 and day 5 progressively reduced its protective effect on stress resistance measured in animals subjected to paraquat on day 10 of adulthood.
source: Again, as with lifespan, delaying the start of mianserin treatment to day 3 and day 5 progressively reduced its protective effect on stress resistance, this time measured in animals subjected to paraquat on day 10 of adulthood (Figure 3d; Table 5).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 3d and Table 5.

claim: Mianserin treatment led to an enhanced transcription of redox genes in response to paraquat as compared to age-matched control animals.
source: Mianserin treatment led to an enhanced transcription of redox genes in response to paraquat as compared to age-matched control animals.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Genes that increased in response to oxidative stress (252) showed a lower expression while genes that decreased (88) in response to oxidative stress showed a higher expression in age-matched mianserin-treated animals.
source: Genes that increased in response to oxidative stress (252) showed a lower expression while genes that decreased (88) in response to oxidative stress showed a higher expression in age-matched mianserin-treated animals (Figure 3e).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 3e.

claim: Mianserin was unable to protect multiple ser-5 mutant alleles (ok3087, tm2647, tm2654) from oxidative stress.
source: Mianserin was unable to protect multiple ser-5 mutant alleles (ok3087, tm2647, tm2654) from oxidative stress (Figure 4a,b; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a; Table 6).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 4a,b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1a, and Table 6.

claim: Mianserin did not protect animals unable to synthesize serotonin (tph-1(mg280)).
source: Furthermore, mianserin did not protect animals unable to synthesize serotonin (tph-1(mg280)) (Figure 4a; Table 6) (Sze et al., 2000).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 4a, Table 6, and a citation.

claim: Seven structurally distinct serotonergic antagonists/inverse agonists also protect from oxidative stress in a ser-5 dependent manner.
source: In addition, seven structurally distinct serotonergic antagonists/inverse agonists also protect from oxidative stress in a ser-5 dependent manner (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b; Table 7).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 4—figure supplement 1b and Table 7.

claim: In N2 samples, mianserin increased the expression of stress response genes that drift down with age (sod-1, sod-2, prdx-2, -3, -6) and decreased the expression of stress response genes that drift up with age (sod-4, sod-5, all hsp-16s), an effect that was not observed in ser-5(ok3087) mutants.
source: In N2 samples, mianserin increased the expression of stress response genes that drift down with age (sod-1, sod-2, prdx-2, -3, -6) and decreased the expression of stress response genes that drift up with age (sod-4, sod-5, all hsp-16s), an effect that was not observed in ser-5(ok3087) mutants.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: SER-3 and SER-4 were dispensable for stress protection and for the attenuation of drift-variance in redox-associated genes.
source: In contrast, SER-3 and SER-4, two receptors we previously showed to be required for lifespan extension by mianserin, were dispensable for stress protection (Figure 4a,b) (Petrascheck et al., 2007), as well as for the attenuation of drift-variance in redox-associated genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 4a,b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c, and a citation.

claim: Young (day 1) wild-type N2 animals and ser-5(ok3087) mutants showed a nearly identical response to oxidative stress.
source: Young (day 1) wild-type N2 animals and ser-5(ok3087) mutants showed a nearly identical response to oxidative stress (Figure 5c).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 5c.

claim: The enhanced response to paraquat by mianserin treatment was ser-5 dependent.
source: The enhanced response was ser-5 dependent (Figure 5d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 5d.

claim: Lifespan-extension by mianserin was strongly reduced or abrogated in ser-5, snt-1 and unc-26 mutant animals.
source: Furthermore, lifespan-extension by mianserin was strongly reduced or abrogated in ser-5, snt-1 and unc-26 mutant animals (Figure 5e, f; Figure 5—figure supplement 1a; Table 8).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 5e, f, Figure 5—figure supplement 1a, and Table 8.

claim: Seven additional serotonergic antagonists/inverse agonists also extended lifespan in a manner that was partially or fully dependent on ser-5.
source: Seven additional serotonergic antagonists/inverse agonists also extended lifespan in a manner that was partially or fully dependent on ser-5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Mianserin-treated animals exhibited a drift-variance slightly lower than that of 3-day-old control animals by day 10.
source: Comparing drift-variances between mianserin-treated and untreated animals, we noticed that by day 10, mianserin-treated animals exhibited a drift-variance slightly lower than that of 3-day-old control animal (P=0.37).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with statistical support.

claim: Mianserin-treated animals showed a ~7–8 day delay in age-associated transcriptional change compared to age-matched controls.
source: This suggested that mianserin-treated animals showed a ~7–8 day delay in age-associated transcriptional change compared to age-matched controls (Figure 2a).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2a.

claim: PCA showed that 10 day-old mianserin-treated animals aligned closer to 3-day-old than to 10-day-old control animals.
source: PCA showed that control samples aligned on the x-axis (dimension 1) according to age and that 10 day-old mianserin-treated animals aligned closer to 3-day-old than to 10-day-old control animals.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding from PCA analysis.

claim: Plotting a mortality curve for over 3,000 mianserin-treated or untreated animals showed a significantly lower mortality level for mianserin-treated animals by day 12.
source: Plotting a mortality curve for over 3,000 mianserin-treated or untreated animals showed a significantly lower mortality level for mianserin-treated animals by day 12 (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6b and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Mianserin treatment decelerated the rise in mortality levels between day 1 and 12 of adulthood.
source: Therefore, mianserin treatment decelerated the rise in mortality levels between day 1 and 12 of adulthood.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion from the mortality curve data.

claim: From day 12 onwards, the mortality curves were parallel showing a 7–8 day shift in mortality across the remaining lifespan.
source: From then on, the mortality curves were parallel showing a 7–8 day shift in mortality across the remaining lifespan.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this observation from the mortality curve data.

claim: The parallel nature of mortality curves suggested that mianserin did not affect mortality rates past day 12 and that its effect on lifespan was restricted to the period of early adulthood.
source: The parallel nature suggested that mianserin did not affect mortality rates past day 12 and that its effect on lifespan was restricted to the period of early adulthood (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a) (Mair et al., 2003; Vaupel, 2010).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this interpretation, referencing Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a, and citations.

claim: Exposing animals to mianserin for 5 or 10 days was sufficient to extend lifespan to the same extent as lifelong exposure.
source: Exposing the animals for 5 or 10 days was sufficient to extend lifespan to the same extent as lifelong exposure (Figure 6c,d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6c,d.

claim: Shorter exposures (8 hr, 1 day) to mianserin also extended lifespan, but not by as much.
source: Shorter exposures (8 hr, 1 day) also extended lifespan, but not by as much, showing that removing mianserin from the culture is an effective means to restrict its action (Figure 6c,d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6c,d.

claim: Mianserin treatment blocks serotonin-induced egg-laying but had a minor effect on amount or timing of spontaneous egg-laying and brood size.
source: Mianserin treatment blocks serotonin-induced egg-laying (Petrascheck et al., 2007), but had a minor effect on amount or timing of spontaneous egg-laying and brood size (Figure 6g).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6g and a citation.

claim: Mianserin did not increase reproductive longevity.
source: Most importantly, mianserin did not increase reproductive longevity (Figure 6g).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6g.

claim: A 24 hr mianserin treatment did not increase the proteasome activity.
source: A 24 hr mianserin treatment did not increase the proteasome activity, as measured by a fluorescence-based assay for chymotrypsin-like activity.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: On day 5, mianserin slightly decreased proteasome activity, consistent with a slight increase in drift-variance in proteasome-related genes.
source: On day 5, mianserin slightly decreased proteasome activity, consistent with a slight increase in drift-variance in proteasome-related genes (Figure 6h; Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6h and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Drift-variance increased in all mouse tissues (brain, kidney, liver, lung, and spleen) with age.
source: Drift-variance increased in all tissues with age (Figure 7a).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 7a.

claim: Plotting drift-variance for each mouse organ as a function of age confirmed that as mice age, drift-variance increases in all organs.
source: Plotting drift-variance for each organ as a function of age confirmed that as mice age, drift-variance increases in all organs (Figure 7b).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 7b.

claim: Over the entire human population, drift-variance remains relatively stable until the age of sixty, and then starts to rise.
source: This analysis shows that over the entire population, drift-variance remains relatively stable until the age of sixty, and then starts to rise (Figure 6c).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6c (likely Figure 7c based on context).

claim: There is a significant correlation (Spearman, rho=0.6, P=0.0014) between age and drift-variance in the human brain.
source: This revealed a significant correlation (Spearman, rho=0.6, P=0.0014) between age and drift-variance in the human brain.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with statistical support.

claim: Fibroblasts from HGPS patients showed increased drift-variance relative to BJ control fibroblasts.
source: As expected for a premature aging syndrome, fibroblasts from HGPS patients showed increased drift-variance relative to BJ control fibroblasts (Figure 7e).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 7e.

claim: Nuclear reprogramming reduced drift-variance in iPSCs to levels closer to those seen in H9 embryonic stem cells.
source: Furthermore, nuclear reprogramming reduced drift-variance in iPSCs to levels closer to those seen in H9 embryonic stem cells.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Increases in drift-variance are reversed by nuclear reprogramming in vitro.
source: Thus, increases in drift-variance are reversed by nuclear reprogramming in vitro
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion from the reprogramming data.

claim: Longevity mechanisms induced by either pharmacologically blocking serotonergic signaling or by blocking insulin signaling by daf-2 RNAi attenuate transcriptional drift.
source: Longevity mechanisms induced by either pharmacologically blocking serotonergic signaling or by blocking insulin signaling by daf-2 RNAi attenuate transcriptional drift (Figure 2a,g).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2a,g.

claim: Abolishing lifespan extension by blocking serotonergic signaling too late (mianserin, day 5) or by addition of daf-16 RNAi (daf-2) abolished the attenuation of drift-variance.
source: Abolishing lifespan extension by these mechanisms by either blocking serotonergic signaling too late (mianserin, day 5) or by addition of daf-16 RNAi (daf-2) abolished the attenuation of drift-variance (Figure 2).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2.

claim: Mianserin-reduced drift-variances are associated with improved stress resistance in older age.
source: Detailed analysis of redox-related pathways showed that mianserin-reduced drift-variances are associated with improved stress resistance in older age (Figure 3).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 3.

claim: Mutations in the serotonin receptor SER-5 that abolish the effect of mianserin on drift-variance also abolished its effect on stress resistance and lifespan.
source: Mutations in the serotonin receptor SER-5 that abolish the effect of mianserin on drift-variance also abolished its effect on stress resistance and lifespan (Figure 4, 5).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 4 and 5.

claim: Mianserin treatment attenuated the age-associated increase of drift-variance, thereby preserving the characteristics of a much younger (~3 days-old) transcriptome up to chronological day 10.
source: Using transcriptome-wide drift-variance values as a metric for age showed that mianserin treatment attenuated the age-associated increase of drift-variance, thereby preserving the characteristics of a much younger (~3 days-old) transcriptome up to chronological day 10 (Figure 2a, 6a).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2a and 6a.

claim: Mianserin caused a 7–8 days delay in age-associated transcriptional change.
source: These results showed that mianserin caused a 7–8 days delay in age-associated transcriptional change and suggested that the physiological changes leading to a lifespan extension were already completed by day 10.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding.

claim: By day 12, the entire mortality curve was shifted parallel by 7–8 days showing that the physiological delay leading to a lifespan extension was already completed.
source: By day 12, the entire mortality curve was shifted parallel by 7–8 days (Figure 6b) showing that the physiological delay leading to a lifespan extension was already completed.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6b.

claim: Mianserin exposure for the first 5–10 days of adulthood was necessary and sufficient to fully extend lifespan.
source: Experiments in which animals were exposed to mianserin for limited periods of time confirmed that mianserin exposure for the first 5–10 days of adulthood was necessary and sufficient to fully extend lifespan (Figure 6c,d).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 6c,d.

claim: Mianserin treatment slows degenerative processes specifically between day 1 and 10, extending the duration of the period of young adulthood thereby postponing the onset of major mortality around mid-life.
source: The most parsimonious explanation that accounts for all these results is that mianserin treatment slows degenerative processes specifically between day 1 and 10, extending the duration of the period of young adulthood thereby postponing the onset of major mortality around mid-life (Figure 6e,f).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as the most parsimonious explanation, referencing Figure 6e,f.

claim: Aging has been shown to cause DNA damage, degeneration of the nuclear architecture, loss of histones, loss of histone modification.
source: Aging has been shown to cause DNA damage, degeneration of the nuclear architecture, loss of histones, loss of histone modification (Kaeberlein et al., 1999; Scaffidi and Misteli, 2006; Burgess et al., 2012).
evidence: The discussion states this as established knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: These changes contribute to the degenerative phenotypes observed with aging.
source: These changes contribute to the degenerative phenotypes observed with aging (Mostoslavsky et al., 2006; Feser et al., 2010; Peleg et al., 2010).
evidence: The discussion states this as established knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: Aging causes the expression of genes within functional groups to drift apart, causing a loss of co-expression patterns as observed in young adults.
source: We found that aging causes the expression of genes within functional groups to drift apart, causing a loss of co-expression patterns as observed in young adults.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: Many physiological processes depend on appropriate stoichiometry of their components.
source: Many physiological processes depend on appropriate stoichiometry of their components.
evidence: The discussion states this as general knowledge.

claim: Large and persistent deviations in mRNA balance as measured by drift-variance are likely to result in stoichiometric imbalances in protein complexes, negatively affecting proteostasis.
source: Large and persistent deviations in mRNA balance as measured by drift-variance are likely to result in stoichiometric imbalances in protein complexes, negatively affecting proteostasis as has been recently observed (Houtkooper et al., 2013; Walther et al., 2015).
evidence: The discussion states this as a likely consequence, supported by citations.

claim: Attenuation of transcriptional drift in the redox system was associated with an improved homeostatic capacity, i.e. an improved ability of the redox system to appropriately respond to outward stimuli.
source: Attenuation of transcriptional drift in the redox system was associated with an improved homoestatic capacity, i.e. an improved ability of the redox system to appropriately respond to outward stimuli.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: Accounting for transcriptional drift effects dramatically simplified what was an initially excessively complex expression pattern.
source: Transcriptional drift also provided a useful concept to analyze aging transcriptomes. Accounting for its effects dramatically simplified what was an initially excessively complex expression pattern (Figure 1).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 1.

claim: Excluding gene expression changes due to drift left a set of genes that changed expression in response to mianserin treatment that was enriched for genes related to stress, innate immunity, aging and the xenobiotic response.
source: Excluding gene expression changes due to drift left a set of genes that changed expression in response to mianserin treatment that was enriched for genes related to stress, innate immunity, aging and the xenobiotic response.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding.

claim: With the exception of the xenobiotic response, all other functions have been linked to serotonin signaling.
source: With the exception of the xenobiotic response, which is expected to be triggered by addition of a foreign substance such as mianserin (Figure 2f), all other functions have been linked to serotonin signaling (Table 1) (Zahn et al., 2006; Petrascheck et al., 2007; Rangaraju et al., 2015a).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this, referencing Figure 2f, Table 1, and citations.

claim: Drift-variance is attenuated by two longevity mechanisms (mianserin and daf-2 RNAi) across large sections of the transcriptome.
source: Further, in accordance with the hypothesis that increases in drift-variance are a signature of aging in the transcriptome, we find that drift-variance is attenuated by two longevity mechanisms (mianserin and daf-2 RNAi) across large sections of the transcriptome.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding.

claim: Many of the age-associated changes that were reversed by mianserin were also reversed by daf-2 RNAi (58%).
source: Many of the age-associated changes that were reversed by mianserin were also reversed by daf-2 RNAi (58%).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding.

claim: Treating daf-2(e1370) mutants with mianserin causes only a partial extension of lifespan (11% instead of 31%).
source: Treating daf-2(e1370) mutants with mianserin causes only a partial extension of lifespan (11% instead of 31%) (Petrascheck et al., 2007) consistent with the idea that many of the genes attenuated by mianserin treatment are already attenuated in daf-2(e1370) mutants and thus do not further contribute to a lifespan extension.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, supported by a citation.

claim: Activation of DAF-16 target genes by daf-2RNAi prevent age-associated drift of thousands of genes, thus resulting in a net decrease of drift, even though a transcriptional program has been induced.
source: Activation of DAF-16 target genes by daf-2RNAi prevent age-associated drift of thousands of genes, thus resulting in a net decrease of drift, even though a transcriptional program has been induced (Figure 2g).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this finding, referencing Figure 2g.

claim: Transcriptional drift is not a biomarker for aging but a metric for aging similar to lifespan measurements.
source: Conceptually, transcriptional drift is not a biomarker for aging. It is a metric for aging similar to lifespan measurements that can be used to monitor age-associated physiological changes on the molecular level within groups of genes.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this conceptual distinction.

claim: Drift-variance allowed monitoring of age-associated physiological changes in young animals, at a time when age-associated mortality levels are too low to be accurately determined.
source: What made drift-variance measures essential for the present study was that it allowed us to monitor age-associated physiological changes in young animals, at a time when age-associated mortality levels are too low to be accurately determined (see below).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this utility of drift-variance.

claim: The finding that transcriptional drift values in mianserin-treated animals already showed a 7–8 day delay in physiological change as early as day 10 suggested a model in which the physiological events responsible for the 7–8 days lifespan extension take place (and conclude) prior to day 10.
source: The finding that transcriptional drift values in mianserin-treated animals already showed a 7–8 day delay in physiological change as early as day 10 suggested a model in which the physiological events responsible for the 7–8 days lifespan extension take place (and conclude) prior to day 10 (Figure 2a, 6a,e).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this interpretation, referencing Figure 2a, 6a,e.

source: In summary, this work describes the phenomenon of transcriptional drift and how it can be used as a metric for aging. Using this metric, we show that blocking serotonergic signals by mianserin delays age-associated physiological changes such as transcriptional drift and mortality exclusively during early adulthood, thus extending the duration of this period and postponing the onset of age-associated mortality.
